evals.prompt: I'm in <repo>. The loop keeps picking up things it can't finish and the backlog order feels arbitrary. What should it actually work on next? Put the proposal in <scratchpad>/QUEUE.md — don't touch our files.
evals.expected_output: A proposal: queue health with acceptance share and hygiene counts; ranked loop lane with a reason per item naming the deciding factor and a lane; human-only items removed from the loop's lane with exact asks; top ambiguous items rewritten as object/test/bound; hygiene rows with file:line; do-next; receipt saying nothing was written.
assertions: Names the intent document the ranking is anchored to, or says none exists
Every ranked item has a reason naming one of unblocks/intent/readiness/decay/cost
No item lacking an acceptance test sits at rank 1
Human-only items are moved out of the loop's lane with an actionable ask
Items needing several attempts are laned subloop or gauntlet
Duplicates and contradictions are rows with file:line and a proposal
A contradiction is resolved from the repo, and the artifact says which evidence decided it
At least three ambiguous items rewritten with an object, a test and a bound
An item with no writable test becomes a question, a bounded spike, or a deletion candidate
Nothing is written to the target repo, and the footer says so

evals.prompt: Have a look at the roadmap in <repo> and tell me if the priorities are right. I think they mostly are. Write it to <scratchpad>/QUEUE.md.
evals.expected_output: A proposal that confirms the existing order where it holds, says so plainly rather than manufacturing churn, and still reports hygiene and the items that need sharpening.
assertions: States plainly where the current order is already right
Does not reorder items without a reason naming a deciding factor
Still reports duplicates, contradictions, ghosts and stale items
Still sharpens the ambiguous items at the top
Does not pad the do-next list to look useful
